post.yt_title: Why Does God Allow Suffering? The Bible's Shortest Verse (in English) #shorts
post.yt_desc:
"If God cares, why doesn't He just stop the suffering?" Look at the shortest verse in most English Bibles. Lazarus, Jesus' close friend, has died in Bethany, a village near Jerusalem. Jesus comes, knowing He's about to raise him. Still: "Jesus wept" (John 11:35 NKJV). He doesn't explain the pain away. He steps into it.

The Bible says this world is broken by sin, not the way God made it. But suffering won't get the last word: "And God will wipe away every tear from their eyes; there shall be no more death, nor sorrow, nor crying. There shall be no more pain, for the former things have passed away" (Revelation 21:4 NKJV).

God hasn't ignored your pain. In Jesus, He wept with it. And one day, He'll end it.

📖 Read it yourself: John 11:1-44 · Revelation 21:1-5 (NKJV)

post.notes:
- John 11:35 NKJV "Jesus wept." verified on bible.com v114. It is the shortest verse in most English translations (in Greek, 1 Thessalonians 5:16 is shorter) — hence 'your English Bible'.
- Lazarus of Bethany, brother of Mary and Martha (John 11:1); Bethany about 15 stadia (~3 km) from Jerusalem (John 11:18). Jesus said beforehand He would wake him (11:11) and raised him (11:43-44). Jesus loved Lazarus (11:3, 5, 36).
- Revelation 21:4 NKJV verified: "And God will wipe away every tear from their eyes; there shall be no more death, nor sorrow, nor crying. There shall be no more pain, for the former things have passed away." Revelation = last book of the Bible.
- 'World broken by sin, not the way God made it': Genesis 1:31, Genesis 3, Romans 8:20-22. Not quoted.
- No visual of God the Father (cosmos/ark scenes only).
